summary: When Nora already looked something up before building you a file, she can hand that along directly instead of re-typing it into a brief.
details: A place's rating, price, or a route's travel time can ride alongside the request as its own data, so the sandboxed builder gets the real numbers rather than a paraphrase.
A map needing a coordinate for an address resolves it inside the sandbox itself, from the address already given — never by asking Nora for a raw position.
Anything that would identify a person or their saved location is refused before the job ever starts, the same way a route request already refuses to reveal someone's home.
limitations: What Nora hands along is her own choice each time — nothing is gathered automatically on her behalf.
Only the data she hands along this way is checked for a person's identity or location. Her own written request to the builder is not screened the same way and is not covered by this.
